description: List positive integers below an exclusive limit whose divisor count is prime and not equal to 2.

source.title: Numbers whose count of divisors is prime
source.algorithm_attribution: Sieve the positive divisor counts, then emit n in increasing order when its count is prime and not 2.
source.implementation_status: Bounded clean-room benchmark; no upstream source code copied

output.semantics: All n in strictly increasing order for which the number of positive divisors of n is prime and is not 2; each n is emitted once.
output.encoding: One little-endian signed 64-bit integer per listed n; no count or terminator is included.
output.success_result: number of bytes written; zero for an empty list
output.null_output_policy: A null output pointer is rejected with -2 even when the valid result is empty.

workspace.meaning: A 1000-element uint16 divisor-count table uses exactly 2000 bytes; the remaining 2096 bytes bound fixed scalar bookkeeping and implementation alignment. Output is caller-owned and written directly after capacity validation.

algorithm_details.primary: Initialize divisor counts to zero and increment each multiple of each divisor d in [1,exclusive_limit). Scan n increasingly and test its count by trial division, excluding count 2.
algorithm_details.independent_reference: For each n, count divisor pairs directly through floor(sqrt(n)); test that result for primality by trial division.
algorithm_details.boundary: The task's baseline strict bound n<1000 is represented by exclusive_limit=1000; lower exclusive limits produce prefixes of the same listed-number set.
algorithm_details.count_bound: For n<1000 the maximum divisor count is below 1000, so uint16 values cannot overflow.
algorithm_details.result_bound: The only qualifying values below 1000 are the 16 prime powers with exponents 2, 4, or 6 listed in the maximum fixture; output is therefore at most 16*8=128 bytes.
algorithm_details.complexity: The primary divisor-count sieve takes O(L log L) increments and O(L) workspace for L=exclusive_limit<=1000; filtering uses O(L sqrt(L)) worst-case trial divisions. The independent divisor-pair reference takes O(L sqrt(L)) time and O(1) auxiliary space beyond its output.
